prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas. Injury: wrist fracture. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1307; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather just go by the name on the case caption, if that's all right.

Q: That's fine. Let's start with the accident itself. Where were you when the collision occurred?

A: I was stopped at a red light on the main road in Pasadena, Texas, in the left lane, waiting to turn.

Q: What were you driving?

A: My sedan. It's a silver four-door, a few years old.

Q: Were you wearing a seatbelt?

A: Yes, always.

Q: Tell me what happened next.

A: I was sitting there with my foot on the brake when I felt a hard jolt from behind. My head snapped forward and then back. The car lurched into the intersection a little bit before I could stop it.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?

A: No. I saw it in my mirror for a second, a pickup, but I didn't have time to react.

Q: After the collision, what did you do?

A: I sat there for a minute trying to catch my breath. My right hand was throbbing. A man from the other car came up and asked if I was okay, and then the police arrived.

Q: When did you first realize your wrist was injured?

A: Almost right away. It swelled up fast, and I couldn't grip anything. I thought it was just a bad sprain at first.

Q: Where did you go for medical care?

A: An ambulance took me to the emergency room. They took X-rays and said the wrist was fractured. They put it in a splint and gave me follow-up instructions.

Q: Have you followed up with a specialist?

A: Yes, I've seen an orthopedic doctor a few times. I had to wear a cast for several weeks, and I'm still doing physical therapy twice a week.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?

A: It's hard to do simple things. I'm right-handed, so I've struggled with cooking, writing, and buttoning my shirt. I had to stop going to my weekend rec league because I can't grip a bat or a racket. Sleeping is uncomfortable too.

Q: Have you been able to return to work?

A: I went back on light duty, but I can't do the lifting I used to do, so I've had to rely on coworkers more than I'd like.
